record.paper_title: Autonomous Agents Modelling Other Agents: A Comprehensive Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can an autonomous agent reconstruct models of another agent's behaviour when the interaction is only partially observable, meaning that observations of environment states and other agents' actions may be incomplete, noisy, or missing, especially in settings where observation probabilities cannot be supplied from domain knowledge in advance?

evidence.quote: Thus, additional research is needed for the development of methods which can effectively reconstruct behaviour models under partial observability, and methods which can deal with partial observability in the absence of domain knowledge.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a sequential interaction between an autonomous learning agent A and one or more other agents acting in a shared stochastic environment. The environment is modelled as a partially observable stochastic game with state space S, joint action space A = A_1 × ... × A_n, transition kernel T(s' | s, a), and, for the learner A, an observation space O together with an observation kernel O(o | s, a). At each time step t, the learner A executes an action and receives an observation o_t ∈ O that may give incomplete, noisy, or missing information about the true environment state s_t and about the actions taken by the other agents. The learner's goal is to reconstruct, from the observation history (o_1, o_2, ..., o_t), behavioural models of the other agents — i.e. policies π_j : H_j → Δ(A_j) (or any equivalent representation such as finite-state controllers, recursive belief hierarchies, or learned function approximators) that predict each other agent j's action given that agent's interaction history H_j.

Develop a general methodology, with provable guarantees, for solving the following problem:

Given only the learner's observation history under such a partially observable stochastic game, and without being supplied a priori with the observation kernel O (so that observation probabilities cannot be assumed known from domain knowledge), construct estimators π̂_j of the other agents' behavioural models such that, as the interaction length grows, π̂_j converges (in an appropriate metric on policies, e.g. expected KL divergence over reachable histories) to the true π_j. Equivalently: characterize identifiability conditions on (T, O, π_1, ..., π_n) under which behavioural models of the other agents are uniquely recoverable from partial, noisy observations when the observation kernel itself is unknown, and provide constructive learning algorithms that achieve this recovery with finite-sample guarantees.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of reconstructing behavioural models of other agents under partial observability — particularly without prior knowledge of observation probabilities — is identified as an outstanding research direction in the agent-modelling literature. Subsequent work has addressed special cases (e.g. I-POMDPs with known observation models, opponent modelling in POMGs with deep learning), but no general solution with identifiability guarantees and unknown observation kernel appears to have been established. The problem appears to remain open.
